questions.prompt: G2 BRIEF — signalpost-swe-bootcamp (you are at U08, where the agent-engineering sequence begins). scripts/check-curriculum.ts validates docs/curriculum/program.json, but the schema parse runs at module top level and nothing tests it. Delegate ONE bounded task to a coding agent: extract the validation into an importable function and add a vitest regression test that a malformed milestone is rejected. Write the brief using the repo's own brief template: goal; current revision; allowed files/actions; boundaries to preserve; excluded scope; test command and acceptance; timebox/stop condition; requested evidence. Commit to your brief first, then tick the checkpoints you covered and add up the weights.

keyPoints.text: [w3] Goal: an exported validate function the CLI still calls, so `npm run curriculum:check` prints the same summary, plus a test that feeds it a milestone missing a required field and expects a rejection.
[w2] Current revision + run record: the brief pins the commit and has the agent record scope, revision, dirty files and verification in docs/runs before it starts.
[w2] Allowed files: scripts/check-curriculum.ts, one new module beside it, and a new test under tests/ (the only place vitest looks).
[w3] Excluded scope: practice/learner and practice/checks are assessed learner work and contracts; the agent must not touch them, and must not edit program.json to make anything pass.
[w2] Boundary: keep the schema's rules exactly (field list, lengths, literals); this is a refactor plus a test, not a schema change.
[w2] Test command and acceptance: `npm test` (vitest run), `npm run typecheck` and `npm run curriculum:check`, all named in the brief with what green means for each.
[w2] Timebox/stop condition and requested evidence: one refactor and one test file, then stop and return the diff plus the exact commands and outputs.

questions.prompt: G2 PRE-MORTEM — same delegation. How does an agent most plausibly go wrong in THIS repo, and which line of your brief prevents it?

keyPoints.text: [w3] It notices failing practice checks and 'fixes' the learner starters, which are intentionally unfinished or defective.
[w2] It runs the full `npm run check`, which also builds the Next.js app, and reports unrelated build failures as blockers.
[w2] It runs the watch-mode test script and never returns, or reaches for the containers suite that needs Docker.
[w2] It tightens the schema while extracting it (strict objects, renamed fields), quietly changing which program files are valid.
[w1] It keeps going into broader scaffolding and the result gets counted as learner progress.

questions.prompt: G2 HANDBACK REVIEW — the agent hands back its diff and a green report. Following the repo's own sequence, what do you do before integrating it?

keyPoints.text: [w3] Inspect the diff, rerun the checks yourself, and explain a failure case with the patch closed.
keyPoints.quote: inspect the diff, run meaningful checks and explain a failure case with the patch closed.

keyPoints.text: [w2] Confirm the CLI's printed summary is unchanged on the real program.json, so the refactor did not alter behaviour.
[w2] Attribute the agent's contribution, resolve any scope creep, and write your own final PR explanation.
keyPoints.quote: attribute the agent's contribution, resolve scope creep and write your own final PR explanation.

keyPoints.text: [w2] The run record carries the exact commands and results, including anything that could not run.
[w1] Afterwards, implement a changed requirement yourself without AI and record the assistance honestly.
keyPoints.quote: implement a changed requirement without AI afterward. Record assistance honestly.
